carrier.sentence: Weekend walking tours led by Rowan visit the restored warehouse district.
A salt-damaged navigation chart gave Mira several weeks of careful repair work.
Retired dock workers shared stories while Tavi recorded their recollections.
Several original roof beams are still visible above the quiet ticket desk.
The eastern gallery was initially a chandlery serving crews from nearby ships.
For the rigging display curators ordered replica rope from a regional workshop.
Courtyard plans may eventually relocate one bench as the young trees mature.
Every stage of roof restoration brought Mira back with a camera.
On clear mornings fishing boats remain beyond the tall windows facing east.
A newly catalogued ledger lets Rowan trace several former ferry companies.
Workers sealed the repaired masonry afterward to limit damage from future storms.
A nineteenth-century mercantile exchange occupied the neighboring brick building for decades.
The surviving winch caption credits Rowan for careful archival research.
Families compare historic maps and recent shoreline photographs beside wide windows.
Recent design notes from Tavi favor muted colors for every display case.
Though modest in scale the generator's output powers a single demonstration lamp.
Many visitors pause beside the detailed model of an original wooden pier.
Near the gallery entrance one central display traces rail service to the docks.
Inside a small donor book each name appears beside a year and hometown.
